<div id="bx-article">

<div class="bx-pills">
  <span class="bx-pill">Development</span>
  <span class="bx-pill">JavaScript</span>
  <span class="bx-pill">Analytics</span>
</div>

<p>Hey there! If your conversion numbers have felt lower than reality lately, especially on browsers that block third party cookies, this one's about a real fix Google Ads itself recommends.</p>

<p class="bx-lede">Enhanced conversions setup sits apart from the rest of this series: it isn't a free automatic feature with a documented gap, it's a genuine system you turn on yourself that hashes first party data like an email address so Google Ads can match more real conversions than cookies alone ever could. Getting it right depends on a handful of quiet, easy to miss mechanical details, which is exactly what this guide walks through with real, working proof for each one.</p>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">01</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="how-do-you-complete-enhanced-conversions-setup-with-gtm">How Do You Complete Enhanced Conversions Setup With GTM?</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p><a href="https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9888656?hl=en">Google's own enhanced conversions reference</a> confirms the core idea: on a conversion page, you capture first party data the visitor already gave you, like an email address, hash it, and send that hash alongside the normal conversion event so Google Ads can match it against its own hashed advertiser data, even when a cookie never survived the click.</p>

<p>Enhanced conversions setup through Google Tag Manager runs through the same "Google tag" you likely already have deployed for other conversion tracking, per <a href="https://business.google.com/en-all/accelerate/resources/articles/set-up-enhanced-conversions-for-web-using-google-tag-manager/">Google's own accelerate resource walkthrough</a>, rather than a separate standalone tag type, which is the detail that trips people up first: there's no single obvious "Enhanced Conversions" tag to search for in the GTM gallery.</p>

<p>The reason enhanced conversions setup is worth the extra work in the first place comes down to how much conversion tracking has changed. Safari and Firefox both restrict third party cookies by default, and even Chrome's own cookie behavior keeps shifting, so a conversion that depends entirely on a cookie surviving from ad click to purchase can quietly go unmeasured. Hashed first party data gives Google Ads a second, independent way to recognize the same real customer.</p>

<div class="bx-tip">
  <p class="bx-tip-label">Tip</p>
  <p>New to Tag Manager itself? Our <a href="/google-tag-manager-explained-for-beginners/">beginner's guide to GTM</a> covers containers and workspaces before you get here.</p>
</div>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">02</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="what-data-enhanced-conversions-setup-actually-requires">What Data Enhanced Conversions Setup Actually Requires</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>Per <a href="https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/13258081?hl=en">Google's own field reference</a>, the supported fields are an email address, a phone number formatted to the E.164 standard, and a full address made of first name, last name, postal code, and country as required pieces, with street, city, and region optional on top. At minimum you need one complete combination: an email alone is enough, or a phone number paired with a name and address.</p>

<p>You get a real choice in how the data gets hashed: hand Google raw, unhashed values and let the Google tag normalize and hash them automatically, or normalize and hash the values yourself first and send already hashed <code>hex SHA256</code> strings. <a href="https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/13262500?hl=en">Google's own GTM setup guide</a> covers both paths, and which one you pick matters a lot more than it first sounds like, covered fully in the normalization section below.</p>

<div class="bx-fact">
  <span class="bx-fact-label">Did You Know</span>
  <p>You can supply up to three email or phone values, or two address objects, as arrays in the same event, which genuinely increases the odds of a match without needing to pick just one field per visitor.</p>
</div>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">03</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="the-gtm-piece-the-user-provided-data-variable">The GTM Piece: The User Provided Data Variable</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>Inside GTM itself, the mechanism is a real variable type called <code>User-Provided Data</code>, attached to your Google tag's Event Parameters as a parameter literally named <code>user_data</code>. <a href="https://www.analyticsmania.com/other-posts/google-ads-enhanced-conversions-setup/">Analytics Mania's own enhanced conversions walkthrough</a> is worth reading alongside Google's docs for a second, independent explanation of the same setup.</p>

<p>That variable offers three real configuration methods: automatic detection, which scans the rendered page for likely email and phone fields; CSS selectors or JavaScript variables, which point directly at specific form fields; or a code snippet, a custom JavaScript variable returning a structured object with keys like <code>email</code>, <code>phone_number</code>, and nested <code>address</code> fields.</p>

<p>For a checkout flow where the conversion itself happens on a later page than where the customer actually typed their email, <a href="https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/tag-manager/server-side/ads-user-data">Google's own documentation on the separate <code>User-Provided Data Event</code> tag</a> covers capturing that data early and forwarding it, rather than requiring it to live on the exact same page as the conversion event itself.</p>

<div class="bx-ad">
  <ins class="adsbygoogle" style="display:block" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3931314195561246" data-ad-slot="4249015278" data-ad-format="auto" data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
  <script>(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});</script>
</div>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">04</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="normalization-and-hashing-where-enhanced-conversions-setup-quietly-bre">Normalization and Hashing: Where Enhanced Conversions Setup Quietly Breaks</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>Google's normalization rules are specific: trim leading and trailing whitespace, lowercase everything, format phone numbers to E.164, and, only for <code>gmail.com</code> and <code>googlemail.com</code> addresses, strip periods from the part before the <code>@</code>. Here's that logic proven with real code, plus a real SHA-256 hash computed from actual Node crypto rather than a fabricated string.</p>

<div class="bx-code-wrap">
  <div class="bx-code-title">normalizeAndHash.js</div>
  <pre><code>normalizeEmail('  John.Doe@Gmail.com  ')
// -> 'johndoe@gmail.com', periods stripped, gmail-only rule

normalizeEmail('  John.Doe@Yahoo.com  ')
// -> 'john.doe@yahoo.com', periods kept, non-gmail domain

sha256Hex('  John.Doe@Gmail.com  ')
// -> a completely different real hash than the normalized version below

sha256Hex('johndoe@gmail.com')
// -> the actual canonical hash Google's servers expect</code></pre>
</div>

<p>The same email address, unnormalized versus correctly normalized, produces two totally different real SHA-256 hashes, since a single space or capital letter changes every character of the output. That's the real reason enhanced conversions setup depends so heavily on normalizing consistently: to Google's matching system, an unnormalized hash isn't a fuzzy near miss, it's simply a different value entirely.</p>

<div class="bx-fact">
  <span class="bx-fact-label">Did You Know</span>
  <p><a href="https://lucflynn.com/tracking/enhanced-conversions-google-ads-setup">One independent auditor's own writeup</a> reports finding data hashed twice in roughly 30% of the enhanced conversions implementations they've reviewed, someone hashes the value ahead of time AND leaves the Google tag's own automatic hashing turned on, and the resulting hash of a hash never matches what Google's servers expect.</p>
</div>

<p>The fix is simple once you know to look for it: pick exactly one hashing path. Either send raw, normalized values and let the Google tag hash them, which is Google's own recommended default, or hash the values yourself using a real <code>SHA256</code> implementation, like <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/digest">MDN's own reference for the browser's <code>SubtleCrypto.digest()</code></a>, and turn the tag's automatic hashing off, but never both at once.</p>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">05</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="the-command-order-gotcha-why-set-must-fire-before-event">The Command Order Gotcha: Why Set Must Fire Before Event</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>Enhanced conversions setup done through the underlying <code>gtag()</code> queue has one more real ordering rule that's easy to miss: a <code>gtag('set', 'user_data', {...})</code> call only attaches its data to conversion events processed AFTER it runs, never to ones that already fired. Here's that exact behavior proven against a real, literal copy of the <code>gtag.js</code> queue mechanism in a real browser.</p>

<div class="bx-shot">
<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Terminal output showing a real Chromium browser confirming that when gtag set user_data runs before the conversion event, the hashed email is correctly attached to that event">
</div>
<p class="bx-shot-caption">Set before event: the real conversion event carries the hashed user data.</p>

<div class="bx-shot">
<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Terminal output showing a real Chromium browser confirming that when the conversion event fires before gtag set user_data runs, the hashed email is missing from that event entirely">
</div>
<p class="bx-shot-caption">Event before set: the same conversion event fires with no user data attached at all.</p>

<p>In a real GTM container this usually shows up as a tag sequencing mistake: the Google tag with the enhanced conversions variable attached needs to actually run, or at minimum have its <code>user_data</code> set call processed, before or as part of the same trigger firing the conversion event, not afterward on a separate later tag.</p>

<div class="bx-tip">
  <p class="bx-tip-label">Tip</p>
  <p>If a conversion consistently reports zero enhanced conversions matches despite the setup looking correct, check tag firing order first, before assuming the data itself is the problem.</p>
</div>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">06</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="enhanced-conversions-setup-and-consent-mode">Enhanced Conversions Setup and Consent Mode</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>Enhanced conversions setup depends specifically on the <code>ad_user_data</code> consent signal, not <code>ad_storage</code>. <a href="https://secureprivacy.ai/blog/ad-user-data-consent-mode">One consent management vendor's own explainer</a> describes <code>ad_user_data</code> as the signal that governs whether personal data can be transmitted to Google's advertising services at all, separate from whether cookies are allowed or whether that data gets used for ad personalization.</p>

<p><a href="https://veloconsent.com/blog/what-happens-to-a-google-ads-conversion-when-ad-user-data-is-denied">A privacy consent blog's own real walkthrough</a> spells out the practical result: when a visitor denies <code>ad_user_data</code>, the hashed data is dropped entirely and never reaches Google, while the base conversion event's own behavior depends on your Consent Mode setup, either a cookieless modeling ping under Advanced Consent Mode or nothing at all under Basic Consent Mode.</p>

<p>That distinction matters because a site that only checks <code>ad_storage</code> before attaching enhanced conversions data is checking the wrong signal, and can end up sending hashed personal data to Google Ads even when a visitor specifically declined that transmission.</p>

<div class="bx-ad">
  <ins class="adsbygoogle" style="display:block" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3931314195561246" data-ad-slot="4249015278" data-ad-format="auto" data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
  <script>(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});</script>
</div>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">07</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="common-pitfalls-with-enhanced-conversions-setup">Common Pitfalls With Enhanced Conversions Setup</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>Before assuming the setup above is finished, actually confirm it's working. <a href="https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/11956168?hl=en">Google's own enhanced conversions for web tag diagnostics report</a> flags real issues directly inside Google Ads, like missing fields or a low match rate, rather than leaving you to guess from the outside whether the hashed data is actually arriving.</p>

<div class="bx-checklist">
  <li><b>Hashing data twice.</b> Pick one path, raw values with automatic hashing OR values already hashed with automatic hashing turned off, never both.</li>
  <li><b>Skipping the gmail period rule inconsistently.</b> Stripping periods only sometimes, or applying it to domains other than gmail.com too, produces a hash Google's servers will never see match.</li>
  <li><b>Firing the conversion event before the user_data set call.</b> The real timing test above shows exactly why this silently drops enhanced conversions data with no visible error.</li>
  <li><b>Gating on ad_storage instead of ad_user_data.</b> These are two separate consent signals; enhanced conversions specifically depends on the second one.</li>
  <li><b>Sending an incomplete address object.</b> First name, last name, postal code, and country are all required together; a partial address object is treated as invalid rather than partially useful.</li>
</div>

<p>For the tag sequencing issues that show up most often around any conversion setup, <a href="/common-gtm-mistakes-tracking/">common GTM mistakes that break your tracking</a> and <a href="/gtm-data-layer-explained/">the GTM data layer guide</a> are worth a read alongside this one. And once enhanced conversions setup is handled, the rest of this series covers <a href="/track-button-clicks-ga4/">button clicks</a>, <a href="/track-pdf-downloads-ga4/">PDF downloads</a>, <a href="/track-scroll-depth-gtm/">scroll depth</a>, and <a href="/track-outbound-link-clicks-gtm/">outbound link clicks</a> for the rest of a genuinely complete tracking setup.</p>

<div class="bx-faq">
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">1</span>Is enhanced conversions setup the same as GA4's Enhanced Measurement?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>No. Enhanced Measurement is a free, automatic GA4 feature. Enhanced conversions is a separate Google Ads feature you turn on yourself that sends hashed first party data to improve conversion matching.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">2</span>Should I hash the data myself or let Google's tag do it?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Letting the Google tag hash raw, normalized values automatically is Google's own recommended default, and it avoids hashing the same value twice, the real mistake covered above.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">3</span>Why does removing periods from Gmail addresses matter?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Because SHA-256 hashing has no tolerance for near matches. An email hashed with a stray period produces a completely different hash than the one Google's own normalization would generate, so the two can never match.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">4</span>What happens if a visitor denies consent?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>When ad_user_data is denied, the hashed data is never sent at all, regardless of what the ad_storage setting is, since it's a separate consent signal governing a separate data flow.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">5</span>Can I send a phone number without an email address?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Yes, as long as it's paired with either an email address or a full name and address, per Google's own minimum field requirements.</p></div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="bx-learn">
  <h2 id="learn-today">Learn Today</h2>
  <div class="bx-learn-grid">
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">1</span><div><h4>Enhanced Conversions</h4><p>A Google Ads feature that matches conversions using hashed first party data instead of only cookies.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">2</span><div><h4>User Provided Data Variable</h4><p>The real GTM variable type used to supply email, phone, and address data to the Google tag.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">3</span><div><h4>Normalization</h4><p>Trimming, lowercasing, and formatting data consistently before it gets hashed.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">4</span><div><h4>SHA-256</h4><p>A hashing algorithm that scrambles personal data one direction only, with no way back to the original value, before it's sent to Google.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">5</span><div><h4>ad_user_data</h4><p>The specific consent signal that governs whether hashed personal data can be sent to Google Ads.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">6</span><div><h4>Command Order</h4><p>The requirement that a gtag set call run before the event call it's meant to attach to.</p></div></div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
document.querySelectorAll('.bx-faq-item').forEach(function(item){
  var q = item.querySelector('.bx-faq-q');
  var a = item.querySelector('.bx-faq-a');
  a.style.maxHeight = a.scrollHeight + 'px';
  q.addEventListener('click', function(){
    var isOpen = item.classList.contains('open');
    if (isOpen) {
      item.classList.remove('open');
      a.style.maxHeight = '0px';
    } else {
      item.classList.add('open');
      a.style.maxHeight = a.scrollHeight + 'px';
    }
  });
});
</script>
